title: The voice in the recording
paragraphs: When Mara found a recording of her grandmother describing life in a mining town, she expected it to settle a family disagreement. Her father remembered his childhood there as unusually secure; his younger sister recalled constant anxiety about money. The recording, made for a local history project, seemed at first to support the father's version. Their mother spoke warmly about neighbors sharing food and looking after one another's children. Mara began selecting extracts for a family gathering.

Listening again, she noticed how often the interviewer interrupted whenever the conversation approached wages or industrial disputes. He was interested in community traditions, and his questions steered the speaker back toward celebrations and mutual help. This did not make the grandmother's affectionate memories false. It did mean that the absence of complaints could not safely be treated as evidence that there had been nothing to complain about. The recording preserved a conversation shaped by two people, not a complete inventory of one person's experience.

Mara asked her aunt to listen before showing the edited version. Her aunt recognized every cheerful incident but supplied details that complicated them. Neighbors had shared food partly because some households could not afford enough. Looking after children had been generous, but it also allowed parents to work unpredictable shifts. The same event could be remembered as solidarity by one child and insecurity by another, without either memory being invented.

For the gathering, Mara included longer passages and left several of the interviewer's questions audible. She also invited both siblings to comment afterward. Her father worried that this would turn a celebration into an argument, but the discussion was gentler than he expected. Nobody withdrew their earlier account. Instead, they began to understand what each account had emphasized. Mara had hoped that the recording would deliver a verdict; it proved more valuable as a starting point for questions that the original interview had never asked.

questions.question: What did Mara initially expect the recording to do?
options: Resolve competing family memories
Expose the interviewer as dishonest
Prove that the town had never existed
Replace the family gathering
questions.evidence: she expected it to settle a family disagreement.
questions.explanation: Początkowo liczyła na rozstrzygnięcie, a nie otwarcie kolejnych pytań.

questions.question: What is the significance of the interviewer's interruptions?
options: They show that every memory was fabricated
They prove the family was wealthy
They made the recording impossible to understand
They limited which parts of the experience were explored
questions.evidence: his questions steered the speaker back toward celebrations and mutual help.
questions.explanation: Kierunek pytań wpływał na zakres zachowanej relacji.

questions.question: How does the aunt's response relate to the grandmother's account?
options: It confirms that nobody faced hardship
It offers an unrelated account of another town
It adds circumstances without denying the events
It rejects every event as false
questions.evidence: Her aunt recognized every cheerful incident but supplied details that complicated them.
questions.explanation: Uzupełnienie kontekstu nie jest zaprzeczeniem opisanych zdarzeń.

questions.question: Why were the interviewer's questions retained in the final version?
options: To prove that the interviewer knew the family
To make the shaping of the account more visible
To make the grandmother appear less reliable
To remove the siblings' opportunity to speak
questions.evidence: left several of the interviewer's questions audible.
questions.explanation: Czytelnik ma wywnioskować, że pytania pomagają usłyszeć, jak powstała relacja.

questions.question: Which interpretation best fits the ending?
options: Understanding can improve without one memory defeating the other
The father finally admitted inventing his childhood
The aunt accepted that money had never been a concern
The recording made further discussion unnecessary
questions.evidence: Nobody withdrew their earlier account. Instead, they began to understand what each account had emphasized.
questions.explanation: Nie nastąpiło jednoznaczne rozstrzygnięcie; poszerzyło się wzajemne zrozumienie.

title: The recommendation she did not send
paragraphs: A former student asked Professor Hale for a recommendation for a research position. He had produced an excellent final project, but during the course he had also missed several deadlines. Hale remembered the frustration vividly and drafted a letter that praised his originality while warning that he needed close supervision. Before sending it, she checked the course records to make sure she was describing a pattern rather than an isolated incident.

The records confirmed the missed deadlines, but they also reminded her that the student had been caring for a sick parent. At the time, he had asked for an extension only once, apparently reluctant to explain the situation repeatedly. Hale had agreed to the extension and then mentally grouped the later delays with ordinary carelessness. Recognizing this did not tell her how dependable he would be in a demanding new role. It did, however, weaken the confidence with which she had been turning past behavior into a stable description of his character.

She contacted him to ask what the position involved and whether he was comfortable discussing the circumstances of that semester. He explained that the role included fixed laboratory shifts, that his care responsibilities had changed, and that he had recently completed an internship. With his permission, Hale spoke to the internship supervisor, who described him as punctual and careful about communicating possible delays. That report was encouraging but covered only a short period and a different kind of work.

Hale rewrote the recommendation. She gave specific examples of the student's analytical strengths, stated when she had taught him, and avoided predictions she could not justify. She did not disclose his family circumstances. The letter was less sweeping than her original draft, but also more informative. To recommend someone responsibly, she concluded, was neither to erase every reservation nor to transform a difficult semester into a permanent verdict. It was to distinguish what she had observed from what she had merely inferred.

questions.question: Why did Hale consult the records?
options: To find private information for the employer
To prove that the project was poor
To avoid writing any recommendation
To check whether her judgment rested on a repeated pattern
questions.evidence: describing a pattern rather than an isolated incident.
questions.explanation: Celem było sprawdzenie podstaw osądu, nie znalezienie pretekstu do odmowy.

questions.question: What did remembering the care responsibilities change?
options: The quality of the student's final project
Her knowledge of his future performance
Her confidence in interpreting delays as a fixed character trait
The dates in the course records
questions.evidence: weaken the confidence with which she had been turning past behavior into a stable description of his character.
questions.explanation: Kontekst zmienił interpretację, a nie same fakty ani pewność co do przyszłości.

questions.question: Why is the internship report treated cautiously?
options: The supervisor had never met the student
It concerned a short period in a different setting
It was anonymous
The student had refused permission
questions.evidence: covered only a short period and a different kind of work.
questions.explanation: Pozytywna opinia ma ograniczony zakres porównywalności.

questions.question: What did Hale leave out of the final letter?
options: The student's family circumstances
All examples of his skills
The period when she taught him
Every factual observation
questions.evidence: She did not disclose his family circumstances.
questions.explanation: Sprawdziła kontekst, ale nie ujawniła prywatnych informacji.

questions.question: What does the passage present as responsible judgment?
options: Avoiding all reservations
Repeating a first impression confidently
Treating every past difficulty as permanent
Separating observed facts from broader assumptions
questions.evidence: distinguish what she had observed from what she had merely inferred.
questions.explanation: Najważniejsze jest oddzielenie obserwacji od wnioskowania.

title: The price of an empty seat
paragraphs: The proposed closure of a night train divided a regional council. On paper, the service looked wasteful: several carriages ran half empty, and the fare revenue covered only a fraction of operating costs. Supporters responded with photographs of students, hospital staff, and elderly travelers who depended on the route. Both sides produced persuasive examples, but neither initially explained what would happen to those passengers if the train disappeared.

An independent transport team examined alternative journeys. Some travelers could switch to daytime trains with little inconvenience. Others would need an extra night in a hotel, miss a shift, or travel by car. For passengers attending early hospital appointments, the apparent replacement service arrived too late. The analysts also found that certain empty carriages could be removed on quiet nights without eliminating the route. This would save less than closure, but more than keeping the timetable and train length unchanged.

The findings did not produce an obvious answer. Counting the cost of a missed shift required assumptions about whose time mattered and how it should be valued. The team made those assumptions explicit and published estimates under several different scenarios. Critics accused it of making the issue unnecessarily complicated. The lead analyst replied that the complications were already present in the journeys; the report had merely stopped hiding them inside a single financial total.

The council approved a reduced service for a year, alongside a booking system intended to match train length to likely demand. It promised to review both expenditure and the journeys people could still make. Campaigners welcomed the reprieve but worried that advance booking would disadvantage passengers whose work schedules changed at short notice. The council added a reserve allocation of seats. The compromise satisfied neither side completely. Yet it shifted the debate from whether an empty seat was inherently wasteful to which transport needs the region was prepared to support and at what cost.

questions.question: What was missing from the initial debate?
options: Examples of people using the train
Any disagreement about closure
A clear account of passengers' realistic alternatives
Evidence that the train cost money
questions.evidence: neither initially explained what would happen to those passengers if the train disappeared.
questions.explanation: Obie strony miały argumenty, lecz nie analizowały dalszych podróży pasażerów.

questions.question: What intermediate option did the analysis identify?
options: Replacing all passengers with freight
Running fewer carriages on quieter nights
Closing every daytime service
Making every journey free
questions.evidence: certain empty carriages could be removed on quiet nights without eliminating the route.
questions.explanation: Można ograniczyć koszt bez całkowitego likwidowania połączenia.

questions.question: How did the analyst defend the report's complexity?
options: It reflected real difficulties rather than creating them
It made the council's decision unnecessary
It proved that costs could not be calculated at all
It deliberately discouraged public debate
questions.evidence: the complications were already present in the journeys
questions.explanation: Złożoność wynikała z rzeczywistości, nie z samego sposobu raportowania.

questions.question: Why was a reserve of seats added?
options: Every carriage was always full
Advance tickets were illegal
Campaigners wanted more photographs
Some passengers could not predict their work schedules early
questions.evidence: work schedules changed at short notice.
questions.explanation: Rezerwa miała chronić osoby bez możliwości planowania z wyprzedzeniem.

questions.question: What changed most in the debate?
options: The council guaranteed the train forever
Campaigners accepted every booking condition
The focus moved from a simple cost symbol to specific needs and trade-offs
Everyone agreed that cost was irrelevant
questions.evidence: which transport needs the region was prepared to support and at what cost.
questions.explanation: Dyskusja stała się bardziej konkretna, ale kompromis nadal miał koszt i ograniczenia.

title: The sentence that would not travel
paragraphs: A publisher commissioned a new English translation of a novel famous for its spare, restrained dialogue. The translator, Inez, encountered a recurring expression that literally referred to leaving a door unlatched. In the original language, it could signal hospitality, reluctance to end an argument, or a refusal to make a final decision. No single English phrase carried all three associations naturally. Repeating the literal image would preserve a visible pattern but risk confusing readers about what the characters meant.

Inez initially chose a different English expression for each occurrence. Her sentences sounded natural, and individual conversations were easier to follow. During a later revision, however, she noticed that a connection between two distant scenes had vanished. Early in the novel, a mother used the expression to welcome her son home; near the end, he used it while postponing an answer to her request. The repeated wording made the second scene echo the first, with an emotional ambiguity that her varied translations had removed.

She experimented with retaining the door image in those two scenes while translating other occurrences more freely. An editor objected that this seemed inconsistent. Inez replied that consistency of wording was not the only kind of consistency a translation could pursue. Her aim was to preserve the relationship between scenes as well as the immediate sense of each line. The editor remained concerned that readers might notice a symbol the original audience would have encountered more casually.

The published version kept the two linked images and included a brief translator's note discussing the decision without proposing a single correct solution. Reviews disagreed about the result. One praised the echo; another found it slightly conspicuous. Inez regarded both reactions as useful evidence about the compromise she had made. Translation, in this instance, had not involved choosing between accuracy and freedom once and for all. It had required deciding which aspect of a sentence's work should be allowed to travel with it.

questions.question: Why was the recurring expression difficult to translate?
options: It appeared only once
Its associations exceeded those of any single natural English equivalent
It referred to an unknown object
The translator did not know its literal meaning
questions.evidence: No single English phrase carried all three associations naturally.
questions.explanation: Problem dotyczył wielu skojarzeń, nie braku znajomości dosłownego znaczenia.

questions.question: What was lost in the first approach?
options: A meaningful echo between distant scenes
The immediate sense of every conversation
All references to family relationships
The order of the novel's events
questions.evidence: a connection between two distant scenes had vanished.
questions.explanation: Naturalne lokalne tłumaczenia osłabiły powiązanie między scenami.

questions.question: What did Inez mean by another kind of consistency?
options: Translating every sentence literally
Making all characters speak alike
Ignoring repeated expressions completely
Preserving relationships and effects rather than identical wording everywhere
questions.evidence: preserve the relationship between scenes as well as the immediate sense of each line.
questions.explanation: Spójność może dotyczyć funkcji i powiązań, nie tylko jednego odpowiednika słownego.

questions.question: What was the editor's remaining concern?
options: The novel had too few notes
The two scenes were unrelated
The English image might draw more attention than the original did
Readers would not know what a door was
questions.evidence: readers might notice a symbol the original audience would have encountered more casually.
questions.explanation: Odtworzenie obrazu mogło zwiększyć jego wyrazistość względem oryginału.

questions.question: What does the final paragraph imply?
options: Freedom and accuracy can always be separated completely
A defensible translation can still involve visible losses and trade-offs
Critical disagreement proves a translation is worthless
A note guarantees universal approval
questions.evidence: useful evidence about the compromise she had made.
questions.explanation: Sprzeczne recenzje ujawniają koszt świadomego kompromisu, nie automatyczną porażkę.

title: The waiting list that grew shorter
paragraphs: A clinic introduced an online system designed to reduce the time patients spent waiting for routine appointments. Instead of being assigned the next available slot, patients could choose among cancellations that appeared throughout the day. Within two months, the average recorded wait had fallen. The clinic celebrated the result, and other services asked whether they could adopt the same software.

A receptionist noticed a less encouraging pattern. Patients who visited the booking page frequently found appointments quickly, while people without reliable internet access continued to call the clinic. Staff could book on their behalf, but the best openings were often gone by the time the telephone line was answered. The system had improved the allocation of some unused slots, yet it had also rewarded the ability to monitor a screen. The average concealed a widening difference between groups.

When the clinic examined the figures more closely, it discovered another complication. The waiting-time calculation began when a booking was successfully made, not when a patient first attempted to obtain one. Someone who spent a week checking the page before finding a slot could appear to have waited only a day. The old system had measured from the initial request. Comparing the two averages without mentioning that change had exaggerated the apparent improvement.

The clinic corrected its report and created a queue for patients who could not repeatedly check the website. Canceled appointments were divided between that queue and the online list. This made the headline average look slightly worse, even as access became more balanced. Some staff found the reversal embarrassing. The receptionist argued that the purpose was not to protect a number but to help patients get appointments. The revised system still saved useful time, but its success was now described through several measures, including unsuccessful booking attempts and differences between patient groups. Those figures were harder to summarize, yet considerably harder to mistake for the whole story.

questions.question: Who benefited most immediately from the new system?
options: Patients able to check the website frequently
Patients who could only call once a week
Everyone equally
Only clinic staff
questions.evidence: Patients who visited the booking page frequently found appointments quickly
questions.explanation: Częste sprawdzanie strony dawało przewagę, więc korzyści nie rozkładały się równo.

questions.question: Why was the comparison with the old average misleading?
options: The old system had no waiting list
All new appointments lasted longer
The clinic measured only emergency patients
The starting point of the measurement had changed
questions.evidence: The old system had measured from the initial request.
questions.explanation: Dawniej liczono od prośby; nowa miara pomijała czas szukania wolnego terminu.

questions.question: What did the new queue aim to address?
options: A legal ban on telephone bookings
The length of medical examinations
Unequal ability to monitor online openings
The absence of any canceled appointments
questions.evidence: patients who could not repeatedly check the website.
questions.explanation: Kolejka wspierała osoby, które nie mogły stale odświeżać strony.

questions.question: Why could a worse headline average accompany an improvement?
options: The clinic stopped collecting data
Fairer access was not fully represented by that average
Every patient began waiting longer
The software was removed entirely
questions.evidence: made the headline average look slightly worse, even as access became more balanced.
questions.explanation: Jedna liczba nie oddaje całego celu: gorsza średnia może współistnieć z bardziej równym dostępem.

questions.question: What is the receptionist's central argument?
options: Measures should serve the service's purpose rather than become its purpose
Statistics should never be published
Online bookings cannot help anyone
Embarrassment is proof of failure
questions.evidence: the purpose was not to protect a number but to help patients get appointments.
questions.explanation: Miernik ma pomagać oceniać usługę, a nie zastępować jej sens.
